strengths: Principled and elegant formulation: bPC naturally unifies top-down generative and bottom-up discriminative processing into a single, well-defined energy objective without artificial stop-gradient operations or biologically implausible weight transport / weight sharing.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The authors evaluate the model across a wide variety of tasks (supervised classification, conditional generation, unsupervised representation learning, joint learning, multimodal association, and perceptual filling-in under severe occlusion) across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100.

Insightful mechanistic analysis: The 2D XOR energy landscape visualisation and MNIST sampling experiments provide a clear and compelling explanation for why bPC succeeds—discriminative and generative objectives act as mutual regularisers, preventing overconfidence (wide minima) and mean-template collapse.

Thorough benchmarking and ablations: The supplementary material is exceptionally detailed, exploring several relevant predictive coding variants (agPC, shared-weight bPC, decay discPC), analyzing the ratio of generative and discriminative weighting hyperparameters, and investigating architectural trade-offs such as max-pooling.

High biological relevance: The model retains local Hebbian plasticity, uses separate error neurons, and exhibits realistic emergent properties such as robust perceptual completion under up to 80% occlusion.
weaknesses: Sensitivity to precision weighting hyperparameters: The balance between discriminative and generative error weights (alpha_disc / alpha_gen) requires significant tuning across different task configurations (differing by several orders of magnitude, e.g., 1 vs 1e-4), which currently limits autonomous self-tuning.

Architectural trade-offs with pooling: In convolutional architectures, pooling in the bottom-up stream induces checkerboard/grid artifacts in the top-down reconstructions; removing max-pooling resolves the visual artifacts but causes a substantial drop in classification performance (~25% drop on CIFAR-10).

Scalability to modern architectures: While evaluation on CIFAR-10/100 with 5-layer CNNs is commendable for the predictive coding literature, PC models still lag behind full backpropagation baselines in terms of training speed and scalability to deeper vision architectures.

strengths: Clear conceptual contribution: The proposed bidirectional predictive coding (bPC) elegantly unifies top-down generative and bottom-up discriminative predictive coding into a single energy function without requiring non-biological weight transport or heuristic stop-gradients (as in hybridPC).

Biologically plausible circuit implementation: The paper clearly details how the inference dynamics and parameter updates map to local neural circuitry featuring distinct value and error neurons with Hebbian plasticity.

Comprehensive empirical benchmarking: The authors evaluate bPC against a comprehensive set of predictive coding and backpropagation baselines (discPC, genPC, hybridPC, agPC, shared-weight PC, AEs, and BP equivalents) across supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised/joint settings.

Insightful mechanistic analysis: The XOR energy landscape visualization and MNIST out-of-distribution / high-confidence sampling experiments provide convincing explanations of why bidirectional constraints regularize the latent space and avoid overconfidence or template-matching bias.

Biological robustness demonstrations: The experiments on multimodal associative learning and robust perceptual filling-in under severe occlusion (up to 80-90% missing pixels) convincingly ground the computational model in cognitive and neurobiological phenomena.
weaknesses: Sensitivity to precision weighting hyperparameters: The balance between discriminative and generative terms (alpha_disc / alpha_gen) requires task-dependent manual tuning, as demonstrated in Appendix D; learning these precision parameters dynamically remains an open problem.

Scale of experimental evaluation: Experiments are restricted to small-scale vision benchmarks (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100); scaling predictive coding models to higher-resolution or modern real-world datasets remains unaddressed.

Generative quality and pooling trade-offs: Convolutional architectures suffer from an architectural trade-off where max-pooling is needed for high classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 but induces grid-like artifacts in generative reconstruction, whereas stride convolutions degrade accuracy substantially.

Computational overhead of iterative inference: Like most predictive coding architectures, bPC incurs substantial computational cost due to running multiple iterative inference steps per sample per batch, which limits training efficiency compared to standard feedforward backpropagation.

strengths: Conceptual and biological relevance: The paper addresses a major limitation in predictive coding (PC) literature—the dichotomy between purely discriminative (feedforward-like) and purely generative (top-down) formulations—by proposing bidirectional predictive coding (bPC) based on a unified energy function with separate bottom-up and top-down weights, preserving local Hebbian plasticity without biologically implausible weight sharing or artificial stop-gradient operations.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The authors benchmark bPC against relevant PC baselines (discPC, genPC, hybridPC, agPC, shared-weight PC) and backpropagation counterparts across a diverse set of tasks: supervised classification, class-conditional generation, unsupervised representation learning, semi-supervised/joint representation learning, multimodal learning, and inference with missing/occluded data.

Insightful mechanistic analysis: The XOR visualization and MNIST energy sampling experiments clearly elucidate why bidirectional learning succeeds: the generative energy constrains and sharpens the overconfident, broad minima of the discriminative loss, while the discriminative term prevents the generative objective from collapsing into degenerate class-mean representations.

Biological demonstrations: The multimodal association cortex modeling and perceptual filling-in / missing information experiments provide compelling evidence for the cognitive and functional advantages of bidirectional predictive architectures over standard feedforward models.

Thorough supplementary material: The appendix provides extensive details on architectures, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization search spaces, compute requirements, ablation studies on loss weighting ratios, and analysis of convolutional pooling artifacts.
weaknesses: Sensitivity to precision weighting hyperparameters: As analyzed in Appendix D, performance strongly depends on the manually tuned scalar weighting ratio between discriminative and generative energies (alpha_disc / alpha_gen). A mismatch can destabilize training or degrade classification accuracy. Making these precisions dynamically learnable would substantially strengthen the biological plausibility and autonomy of the model.

Architectural trade-offs with convolutional operations: Integrating max-pooling in the bottom-up stream induces noticeable grid artifacts in the top-down reconstructions (Figure 5C). Removing max-pooling mitigates artifacts but leads to a substantial degradation in classification accuracy (~25% drop on CIFAR-10, Table 15), revealing a structural friction between standard CNN operators and bidirectional inference.

Computational overhead and inference latency: Iterative energy minimization requires substantial inference iterations during both training and evaluation (e.g., up to 100 inference steps for classification/generation and 600k steps in the occlusion convergence analysis), which remains computationally demanding compared to standard amortized or purely feedforward architectures.

strengths: Clear conceptual framework and strong biological motivation: The paper addresses a prominent dilemma in predictive coding (PC) between feedforward discriminative models and feedback generative models by cleanly unifying them under a single, biologically plausible energy minimization objective.

Extensive and rigorous experimental validation: The authors evaluate bPC across a wide variety of tasks—supervised classification, conditional generation, unsupervised representation learning, stochastic distribution sampling (FID), multimodal association, and robustness to occlusion—across multiple datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet).

Scaling to deep architectures: Unlike many predictive coding studies restricted to small MLPs, this work scales PC to deep convolutional architectures (VGG-5, VGG-9, VGG-16) on Tiny-ImageNet using recent error-optimization techniques, demonstrating significant robustness advantages over standard BP and discriminative PC under severe occlusion.

Insightful mechanistic analysis: The visualization and analysis of the energy landscapes on XOR and MNIST provide clear intuition on how bidirectional constraints prevent both the overconfident, wide minima of discPC and the over-concentrated class-mean collapse of genPC.

Thorough supplementary material: The appendix provides extensive parameter-matched experiments, ablations on the precision weighting ratio ($\alpha_{disc} / \alpha_{gen}$), analysis of pooling artifacts, and detailed training protocols.
weaknesses: Heuristic precision balancing: The weighting parameters $\alpha_{gen}$ and $\alpha_{disc}$ require substantial task- and architecture-dependent manual tuning (e.g., $\alpha_{gen}$ dropping to $10^{-8}$ in VGG-16). In classical PC theory, precisions are dynamically inferred or learned; having them fixed and tuned via grid search diminishes some theoretical elegance.

High computational cost during inference: Handling missing information requires an immense number of iterative inference steps (up to 600,000 steps in MLPs or a multi-stage heuristic with 3,000 steps in VGGs), making inference computationally demanding compared to feedforward or standard amortized models.

Generative quality limitations on natural images: While bPC achieves solid classification and reconstruction RMSE, the qualitative reconstructions on complex natural images (CIFAR-10/Tiny-ImageNet) remain somewhat blurry or exhibit pooling/deconvolution artifacts, lagging behind dedicated generative architectures like VAEs or diffusion models.

strengths: Conceptual elegance and biological plausibility: bPC elegantly unifies generative (top-down) and discriminative (bottom-up) predictive coding into a single energy function with local Hebbian learning rules, without requiring non-biological weight transport or non-local backpropagation.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors validate the model across a wide spectrum of computational tasks, including supervised classification, class-conditional generation, unsupervised representation learning, Langevin-based generative sampling, and multimodal association.

Insightful analysis of the energy landscape: The XOR visualization and low-energy MNIST sampling offer a clear and compelling explanation for why unidirectional models fail (discPC yields broad, overconfident minima admitting nonsensical inputs, while genPC collapses to class means) and how bidirectional coupling resolves these failure modes.

Successful scaling to deeper networks: Unlike many predictive coding studies restricted to small MLPs on MNIST, this work evaluates deeper convolutional architectures (up to VGG-16 on Tiny-ImageNet) and convincingly demonstrates superior robustness against severe pixel occlusion (30-50% missing data) compared to standard feedforward and discriminative PC baselines.
weaknesses: Sensitivity and heavy reliance on the weighting hyperparameter ratio: The performance of bPC heavily depends on the balance between discriminative and generative terms (alpha_disc / alpha_gen). In deeper networks, this ratio spans orders of magnitude (ranging down to 1e-8 for VGG-16), requiring extensive tuning rather than emerging dynamically via learned precisions.

Heuristic inference schedule for deep networks with missing inputs: For the deeper models (Section 4.6 and SM I), inference under missing input conditions relies on an ad-hoc two-stage procedure (1,000 warm-up steps with alpha_disc = 0 followed by 2,000 steps with alpha_disc = 1) totaling 3,000 steps, which somewhat departs from the clean, unified biological dynamics proposed in Section 3.

Architectural trade-offs with pooling operations: As discussed in Section 4.3 and SM E, max-pooling in the discriminative pathway causes notable checkerboard/grid artifacts in the generative reconstruction pathway, while removing pooling hurts discriminative accuracy significantly (dropping classification accuracy by ~25% on CIFAR-10).

strengths: Principled and biologically plausible formulation: The paper neatly unifies discriminative and generative predictive coding into a single scalar energy function, preserving local Hebbian plasticity without requiring non-local error propagation or biologically implausible weight sharing between feedforward and feedback paths.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The proposed bPC is benchmarked across an extensive range of settings—supervised classification, conditional generation, unsupervised representation learning, stochastic distribution sampling (FID), bimodal association, and robust classification under heavy input occlusion (up to 90% missing pixels).

Insightful analysis of the energy landscape: The XOR visualization and the energy-threshold sampling experiments provide clear intuitive and empirical justifications for why discPC yields overconfident out-of-distribution minima and why genPC over-concentrates around class means, highlighting how bidirectional coupling regularizes the landscape.

Thorough benchmarking and scaling: The evaluation includes appropriate biological baselines (genPC, discPC, hybridPC, agPC) as well as backpropagation counterparts, incorporates parameter-matched controls in the appendix, and demonstrates scalability up to VGG-16 on Tiny-ImageNet using error optimization.
weaknesses: High sensitivity and heuristic tuning of precision/weighting parameters: The relative balance between discriminative and generative energy terms (alpha_disc and alpha_gen) varies dramatically across architectures and datasets (e.g., ranging down to 1e-8 for deeper models), requiring task-specific manual search rather than being learned adaptively as true dynamic precisions.

Substantial computational overhead during inference: Although feedforward initialization mitigates inference latency, the network still requires iterative inference steps (hundreds to thousands of steps for occlusion/deep models), making training and evaluation significantly slower and more resource-intensive than standard feedforward networks.

Structural trade-off with pooling operations: As acknowledged in Section 4.3 and Appendix E, standard pooling layers introduce pronounced checkerboard artifacts in the generative top-down path. Eliminating pooling remedies the generative quality but results in a significant drop in classification accuracy (~25% on CIFAR-10), indicating an unresolved tension between feedforward spatial invariance and generative reconstruction.

Evaluation remains constrained to moderate-scale tasks: While scaling to Tiny-ImageNet with VGG-16 is a notable step forward within the predictive coding literature, the framework has not yet been demonstrated on full-scale benchmarks (e.g., standard ImageNet-1k) or modern residual/attention-based architectures.
